# Now 2.13.82
- Swiping to the next or previous song on YouTube Music shows the incoming cover again. The script that reads the queue was being collapsed onto a single line before it was sent to the browser, so the first comment in it commented out the rest of the script, including its final line — a syntax error, which meant the probe never returned anything and it looked as though the site had changed its markup. Line structure is now preserved on the way to the browser, so this cannot happen again to any of these scripts. - That preview artwork is no longer a blurred thumbnail. The queue only publishes a 60-pixel cover, which was being stretched to fill the tile; Now asks for the same 544-pixel square the player bar already uses for the current track, so the incoming and outgoing covers match mid-swipe.

# Now 2.13.81
- Spotify in the browser is detected again. Spotify's web player runs its audio through Web Audio rather than a page media element, and it never publishes a playback state to the system, so Now read every Spotify tab as paused at 0:00 — which meant it lost to any other music tab, and on its own showed a stalled track with no progress. Position, length and play state are now read from the player bar instead: the overlay follows the song, the progress bar and synced lyrics track it to the millisecond, and the cover art comes through at full resolution rather than as a 300-pixel thumbnail. - Play, pause and seeking work on Spotify web. Play and pause check the current state before acting, so pressing play on an already-playing tab no longer pauses it, and scrubbing — including clicking a lyric line to jump — seeks to the exact position rather than the nearest five seconds. - Apple Podcasts transcripts have been removed. They needed Full Disk Access, the timing had to be nudged by hand for each episode, and a wall of speech never scrolled as smoothly as song lyrics. Podcast playback itself is unaffected — episodes still appear in the widget and in the full-screen view. Now no longer asks for Full Disk Access at all.

# Now 2.13.80
- Podcast transcripts now keep pace with the voice. Apple Podcasts only reports its playback position to the system occasionally, so the position available to Now trails the audio and the transcript trailed with it. Measured against Apple's own transcript view, its highlighted line sat between four and six seconds ahead of the position shown on the same screen. The transcript is now brought forward to compensate, with a Sync control under Lyrics in Settings to fine tune it, since the gap varies by episode and with inserted advertising.
